title: fix(update): keep stale-plugin refresh out of the candidate canary deadline
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes candidate Gateway validation spending its startup budget refreshing stale plugins in a disposable state snapshot, then reporting a stopped SQLite integrity worker as a startup failure.

Fixes #148614. Reported by @aaronqianaa (#148614).

## User Impact

Candidate startup verifies copied plugin payloads without downloading replacements and warns that live update finalization owns the refresh. Missing copied payloads remain warnings in the isolated canary. An accepted Gateway stop joins cleanup without misclassifying a SIGTERM/SIGINT-interrupted check as database failure; real integrity verdicts, SIGKILL, and cleanup failures still fail.

The candidate-side changes recognize isolation markers already set by the installed 2026.9.3 updater, protecting that first hop. The new explicit validation-deadline log is updater-side and applies once this updater is installed. No new configuration, schema, dependency, or retention changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [shipped updater](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.3/src/infra/update-candidate-canary.ts#L112) shares a capped five-minute budget across snapshot, Doctor, lint, config/plugin checks, and Gateway startup. Gateway preflight invokes post-core convergence before its first `loading configuration…` log; convergence can download a replacement only into the disposable snapshot. Repeated validations therefore repeat work that live finalization already owns.

The reported 298-second failed-step duration is the whole validation duration, not Gateway process uptime. In the final attempt, migration continuation finished at 16:34:32.200 and the Gateway's first log arrived at 16:35:42.016: approximately 70 seconds of Gateway pre-log work, with earlier validation consuming the rest. The transcript does not establish that all 4.5 minutes were a registry fetch. Main already replaced the fixed default with state-sized budgets; this change preserves that owner.

The old updater sends SIGTERM to the whole process group. An integrity child's separate admission signal can remain live when that signal kills it. The supervisor now preserves the interruption type, and the run-loop recognizes it only while settling an accepted stop.

## Evidence

- All five focused owner suites passed: 248 tests across canary, integrity, run-loop, startup preflight, and plugin verification. Existing budget tests cover a snapshot longer than five minutes and state-sized runtime allowances.
- Before/after regressions: preflight reached network convergence before the fix; an unavailable copied plugin blocked before the fix; a stopped integrity worker produced a generic failure and `startup_failed` before the fix. All pass after the owner repairs.
- Native macOS self-SIGTERM proof failed before and passed after. The committed supervisor regression uses a portable close-event fixture; run-loop tests preserve cleanup failure and SIGKILL behavior.
- `pnpm build` passed. A real built-CLI canary with a stale-channel-descriptor plugin, accepted fixture capabilities, and a registry configured to delay responses by 310 seconds reached readiness in 30.4 seconds, made zero registry requests, loaded the fixture plugin, emitted the deferral warning, and shut down cleanly.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed after correcting two test lint issues; no baselines or suppressions changed. Production delta: +50 lines net.
- [Published 2026.9.3 package-update acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34920008805) passed against exact source `c0e04d0f4799654418a7fbb53dd08d6d3efc467b`, with workflow tooling pinned to `98b321fce638620713efafb39f85fbec3bde5fce`. The `configured-plugin-installs` cell passed on its first attempt in 291 seconds using the published updater. Captured first-hop finalization returned `ok`, repaired brave/codex/discord/matrix to the candidate version, and reported no warnings, sync errors, or integrity drift. Automatic migration, configuration validation, state-survival assertions, Gateway health/readiness, and status passed. This cell uses manual restart; it does not prove service-managed restart.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34919984848) passed on attempt 2. The sole initial failure was the unrelated browser relay `read ECONNRESET` in bundle-11; it passed on the one authorized failed-job rerun. No test or production code changed for the rerun.


Known limits: the exact core target in the reporter's attempt remains unknown. `--timeout` cannot override the 2026.9.3 canary cap. No plugin-only one-hop workaround is claimed: `plugins update codex` exists, but its version selection uses the installed core and does not prove the candidate-matched plugin is prepared. The EPIPE stack is unavailable; the canary has ignored stdin, so no speculative pipe-write fix is included. No issue comments were posted.

## ClawSweeper review

The completed review of `c0e04d0f479` identified no introduced code defect. Its published-driver merge-risk, live plugin outcome, and upgrade-compatibility proof requests are addressed by the successful acceptance run and inspected artifact above. The data-model heuristic requires no schema change: this PR changes candidate preflight and interruption classification, and the upgrade cell passed automatic migration and state-survival checks. No code fixups were needed; no re-review was requested because the code is unchanged.
